chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: Bunk Johnson's legend: circus, New Iberia and the cap on the side
summary: Bunk went with circuses, ended up in New Iberia where Milt and Danny found him, and was admired in parades with a girl holding his horn.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Bunk Johnson was there playing second fiddle to Evan Thomas. Bunk Johnson split from there, and went on the
He went on the circus. Then he went with the (?)Shell Float(?) touring, that other circus, that went all over the world.

Yeah, and he come back to New Iberia, and stayed out there. He was a legend in (?) parts. That son-of-a-bitch, boy, you should have heard that man. Bunk Johnson! King Oliver, none of them was playing that shit then. See, he wasn't powerful, but the shit he played on his horn. See, he was always running that third valve. See, you can't (?) that very few trumpet players play with that third valve. That's where you get them accidental (?) sharps in your line.
Well, when we were with Cab Calloway, you took me back up in (?), where we found him back up there.
I took pictures of him there. I still have those pictures.
You took me down there on one of the (?) ways. That's amazing.

So that's the legendary Bunk Johnson. (?) used to be in the parade with him. He said King Oliver had a funny eye. He said, "you bad-eyed sumbitch, you won't listen when I'm playing!" He was a little sassy, ratty(?) or something, tatty... (?) tells me he'd wear his cap on the side. Everybody got their position of the cap...

Yeah. He's got his cap on the side! And he got hold of one of the chicks to hold his horn, and another one holding his bottle. And that's how he walked in the parade. And everybody was looking at Bunk. That's a helluva a thing, man, to see that. When you'd hear, like, Lee Collins and them would play...
